title: August 2026
campaignIntro: This SEO growth initiative is focused on strengthening Oatley Vigmond’s visibility across Google Search, Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini, and other emerging AI-powered search platforms.

Our ongoing work includes technical SEO, AI search optimization (AEO), geographic search optimization (GEO), content architecture, internal linking, conversion tracking, and marketing automation to increase qualified case inquiries across Ontario.
monthlyRecap: August focused on improving the site’s technical foundation, crawl efficiency, content relationships, and semantic clarity. We cleaned up the XML sitemap, strengthened internal links across key legal content, refined legacy redirects, improved the homepage heading hierarchy, and enhanced the accessibility tree so search engines, screen readers, and AI-based agents can interpret the site more clearly.

recap: August’s audit maintains a 100/100 on-page SEO score, with organic monthly traffic at 6,109, 1,932 organic keywords, and 5,161 backlinks. The audit crawled 9,597 pages and identified 48 issues.

internalLinks.details: Audited redirected, outdated, and unnecessary URLs, then removed pages that should no longer be submitted to search engines.
Strengthened links between key practice areas, expertise pages, lawyer profiles, and supporting content to improve crawl paths, authority flow, and topical relationships.
Reviewed older and retired URLs and replaced broad or less-relevant redirects with the most appropriate current practice-area or expertise pages.
Improved the H1/H2/H3 hierarchy with descriptive, search-focused headings that better communicate the firm’s services and expertise.

internalLinks.task: Accessibility tree and AI crawler improvements
internalLinks.details: Improved semantic page structure and accessibility markup so Google, screen readers, and AI-based agents can interpret primary content, headings, navigation, links, and page relationships more clearly.

nextSteps: In September, we will extend the internal-linking strategy beyond the initial Brain Injury and Catastrophic Injury work. We will identify additional high-value practice areas, expertise pages, lawyer profiles, and supporting resources, then build more relevant contextual links to strengthen crawl paths, topical authority, and the flow of page authority across the site.

We will continue the technical SEO and accessibility review by auditing heading structure across priority pages, correcting H1/H2/H3 hierarchy where needed, and identifying further crawl, redirect, sitemap, canonical, and indexability issues. This work will help Google, screen readers, and AI-based agents interpret the site’s primary content and page relationships more consistently.

We will review and strengthen structured data where it is appropriate, with particular attention to organization, legal-service, attorney, FAQ, article, and practice-area schema. We will also assess WebMCP readiness and opportunities so the site remains prepared for emerging AI-agent and tool-enabled search experiences while maintaining clear user controls and reliable information architecture.
